summary.headline: RBZ Q2 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR 225 crore, but PAT fell to INR 16 crore (7.3% margin) on Surat store carrying costs and lower gross margin.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 55% YoY to INR 225 crore, led by Retail at INR 148 crore (+72% YoY), with Wholesale up 31% and Job Work at about INR 3.3 crore (+19%). EBITDA rose 3.5% YoY to INR 29 crore, with margin at about 13%, while PAT was INR 16 crore (7.3% margin) versus about 12% a year earlier. Management attributed the profit squeeze to the Surat store opening at end-September: finance cost rose from INR 2.55 crore to INR 5.54 crore due to inventory carrying cost, depreciation rose from INR 86 lakh to INR 1.7 crore, and one-time promotion expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore. Gross margin fell on a higher bullion sale component linked to vendor payments, which management said carries near-zero profit.

financial_highlights.value: not stated; management said it declined
financial_highlights.change: Shikhar cited about 6% decline YoY, not confirmed by management

segments.name: Retail (Harit Zaveri Jewellers)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 148 crore, up 72% YoY, and the key growth driver; volume 96 kg versus about 80 kg a year ago. Surat store opened end-September and is averaging about INR 50 lakh of jewellery sales a day, with average ticket size INR 3.5-4 lakh.

segments.name: Wholesale (B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 31% YoY; volume 47 kg in Q2. Management said B2B will remain stable with no signs of decline in gross value of merchandise, while growth shifts to B2C.

segments.name: Job Work
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR 3.3 crore, up 19% YoY; volume 219 kg in Q2. Management could not split Job Work contribution to PAT; said Navratri shift (Sept 22 to Oct 11) delayed deliveries and October volume would be about 100 kg versus about 50 kg a year ago.

guidance_outlook: Retail expansion: Rajkot store launch targeted 21-25 November 2026 (third week of November), Maninagar in December and Gandhinagar in January; about 3-4 store openings per year.
Marketing spend of INR 20-25 crore expected this year for new store rollouts.
Store economics: capex of INR 10-15 crore per large-format store, excluding inventory of about INR 150 crore; capex breakeven targeted within about 1 year.
Inventory turns: about 1 turn TTM currently, targeted 1.75 then 2.25 for mature stores; year-one turn 1-1.2x, 2-2.5x by year three.
Blended retail gross margin around 14% (range 14-16% if studded ratio rises); consolidated EBITDA margin of 11-12% sustainable if services remain stable, per management.

Gold metal loan (GML): currently about INR 14-15 crore (about 14-15 kg); target about INR 100-150 crore (about 100 kg) by Q1 FY28; management aims to hedge inventory within 2-2.5 years and see debt-equity leverage around 2:1.
capex_capacity: Surat store opened end-September 2026 with a new Surat floor including lightweight/low-carat segment; Vicky Kaushal inaugurated the store.
Rajkot store is a 3-storey format, a couple of thousand sq ft larger than Surat; launch slipped from the planned 1 November to the third week of November.
Manufacturing: state-of-art facility with casting, laser and 3D printing; 200+ professionals and about 250 artisans.
Management cited participation in 5 jewellery exhibitions during the quarter (Saurashtra, North Gujarat, Ahmedabad).
demand_pricing: Surat store averaging about INR 50 lakh of jewellery sales per day (excluding bullion and coins) in its first month, with no discounts; management said walk-ins strong but conversion challenged in early weeks.

Gross margin decline attributed to bullion sales linked to paying vendors via gold during B2B-to-B2C stock transfer; management said bullion carries near-zero profit and gross margin will be affected until this normalises.
Management said there is no inventory loss; gold has depreciated but gains were limited.
Harit Zaveri Jewellers in Ahmedabad and Surat; management claims about 20 years of wholesale and manufacturing experience, serving 72 cities, 300 mom-and-pop stores and major corporates.
Management said gold price spikes or dips typically normalise demand within about one week.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the YoY margin drop is from gold prices versus new store expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no inventory loss; limited gold gain. Finance cost rose to INR 5.54 crore from INR 2.55 crore due to inventory carrying cost of about 2.5 months before Surat sales started; depreciation rose to INR 1.7 crore; one-time promotion expenses rose by INR 5-6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What volume split exists between Retail, Wholesale and Job Work?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 volumes: Retail 96 kg, Wholesale 47 kg, Job Work 219 kg, total about 364 kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GML exposure and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently about INR 14-15 crore (14-15 kg); target about 100 kg, by Q1 FY28 at the latest. Later clarified as INR 100-150 crore minimum by next Q1 call.

qa_highlights.question: What are the store-level KPIs and breakeven timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Metrics are footfall, conversion ratio, sales and ticket size. Capex breakeven targeted within a maximum of one year, excluding inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term store count and margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3-4 openings a year, with no 2030 number given; consolidated EBITDA margin of 11-12% sustainable if services remain stable, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What are marketing plans and how is the Surat store performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing of INR 20-25 crore planned this year. Surat is doing about half of Ahmedabad store's annual run-rate; management did not quantify bullion sales within retail revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Job Work and Wholesale volumes dip, and what about GML and the gold price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to the Navratri shift (Sept 22 to Oct 11), with October normal; Q3 expected to give better clarity. GML is 2-3% of borrowings per management, with GML rates about 3.5-4% versus CC about 9%; management said it only hedges the gold commodity component and gave no explicit price outlook.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from bullion sales linked to the B2B-to-B2C stock transfer; management did not quantify bullion sales or the gross margin figure.
Surat store conversion and store economics: management cited early conversion challenges and capex breakeven within one year, with inventory of about INR 150 crore per large-format store.
Working capital and leverage: GML only 2-3% of borrowings currently; plan to raise it to about 100 kg by Q1 FY28 and to 2:1 debt-to-equity implies higher borrowings.
Rajkot launch slipped from 1 November to the third week of November, missing the Diwali season.
Management could not split Job Work contribution to PAT; Q2 PAT margin fell to 7.3%.
Ahmedabad vs Surat retail figures, and bullion share in retail sales, not disclosed; same-store sales growth to be assessed at Q3.
summary.management_tone: Confident on retail demand and expansion, but defensive on margins: management repeatedly attributed the PAT decline to one-off store-opening costs and bullion-sale mix, and declined to quantify several items (bullion sales, Job Work PAT, gross margin).
key_quotes: Retail has been the leader in terms of driver and the upside.
B2C is where you will see a primary kick in will happen, the growth will happen.
So, a consolidated level, yes, if the services remain same, we can sustain that.
